text:
navid: hey team — quick check: after rotating a service API key into GH Secrets, our streaming client suddenly started throwing 401s. key is used as a Basic auth header. any quick ideas?

mia: ugh, maybe a hidden char. did you paste from docs or slack? non-breaking/spaces or ZERO-WIDTH stuff can sneak in. :face_with_monocle:

sam: can you print the exact bytes of the secret in the running container? quick command:```bash
echo -n "$API_KEY" | xxd -p -c 256
```that'll show if there's an extra 0a/20/efbbbf etc.

navid: good point — pasted from an email thread. running that now...

navid: output shows: `6162636465660a` (so there's a 0a at the end). looks like newline.

mia: yep newline. many clients include the header verbatim. Basic header should be `Authorization: Basic $(echo -n "$KEY" | base64)`. if key has trailing `\n` you'll encode it too and server rejects.

sam: for a quick fix in GH Actions, use `echo -n \"$SECRET\"` or set `trim: true` in the action if using any wrappers. alternatively:```bash
clean_key=$(printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" )
# or
clean_key=$(echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | tr -d '\r\n')
```then build header:```bash
header=$(printf '%s' \"$clean_key\" | base64)
curl -H \"Authorization: Basic $header\" ...
```

navid: thanks — that did it. we had a trailing newline in the GH secret because someone pasted with enter. streaming client in ruby didn't trim and we sent invalid header.

mia: fyi node-fetch will also not strip by default, but some SDK helpers sometimes call `trim()` before encode — so behavior differs between libs. good to normalize on our side.

sam: might be worth adding a one-liner check in our quickstart: `printf '%s' \"$REDWOOD_API_KEY\" | xxd -p` and a note: \"no trailing whitespace/newlines.\"

ci-bot: secret redwood-service-key rotated by @navid — rollout started.

navid: adding short note to auth docs and a GH Actions snippet to trim. thanks all. :thumbsup:
